subject: Mutual action plan & evaluation: capacity handoff for HealthSync
messages:

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan kickoff — HealthSync evaluation

Thanks for the kickoff earlier today. A couple of clarifying questions from our infra and procurement teams so we can align the MAP with our timelines:

1) Lead times: we heard ~10-12 weeks for private on-prem GPU pools vs ~4-6 weeks for VPC/dedicated. Can you confirm assumed lead times and what drives the delta?
2) Pool sizing: during eval we expect up to 300 concurrent inference slots at 4 tokens/sec on average — what GPU count / instance mix should we plan for in an initial committed pool?
3) Acceptance criteria: procurement wants the acceptance checklist up front (SLA, SOC2 evidence, audit logs, data residency). Can you attach the specific gating docs?

We attached our internal timeline and procurement template. Can we get a consolidated M.A.P. that maps evaluation milestones to procurement milestones so finance can plan?

—Sienna
Head of Platform, HealthSync

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Sienna Park <sienna@healthsync.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan kickoff — HealthSync evaluation

Hi Sienna — thanks, and great questions. I summarized answers below and attached a draft MAP that ties evaluation gates to procurement milestones (see HS-MAP-v1.xlsx). High-level answers first — details in the MAP and attached acceptance checklist (HS-Eval-criteria.pdf).

Lead times (typical):
- Private/on-prem (air-gapped or customer datacenter): 10–14 weeks from signed order. Drivers: hardware procurement lead time, onsite racks/networking, and customer acceptance window for air-gapped installs.
- Redwood Private (VPC-deployed but customer-controlled network): 6–8 weeks — faster because we pre-provision AMIs and do less physical staging.
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed dedicated GPU pools): 3–6 weeks for initial tranches when inventory available; may be impacted by H100 supply.

Initial pool sizing guidance (rule-of-thumb):
- Target 300 concurrent slots @ 4 tok/s -> ~1.2k tok/s sustained. For generation models with caching and batching, we recommend starting with 16 H100-equivalent GPUs (mixed single-card/4-card pods possible) + autoscale headroom.
- We include a modeling sheet in the MAP that shows expected p95 latency and nominal throughput across 8/12/16/24 GPU pool sizes.

Acceptance gates we attach: SLA targets, SOC 2 evidence checklist, log retention & syslog/export examples, and handoff runbooks. Procurement template: we reviewed the PO template you sent and added a minimal acceptance appendix (attached).

Next steps I propose:
1) We (Redwood) update the MAP with your final eval test cases by 2026-10-05.
2) Procurement review the PO template and confirm commercial points by 2026-10-08.
3) We schedule a joint infra sync (30 min) the week of 2026-10-11 to finalize on-prem vs VPC decision and lock lead-time assumptions.

I've copied Karthik for capacity modeling and Laura for onboarding/acceptance. If that timeline looks tight, call it out and we'll adjust.

Best,
Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-10-05T14:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan kickoff — HealthSync evaluation

Sienna — following up with the capacity model output and a quick sanity-check on the assumptions we used in HS-MAP-v1.xlsx:

Assumptions used for the initial committed tranche: 
- Baseline model: 13B opt-model family, avg output 750 tokens/session, 4 tok/s generation rate, KV cache hit rate 18% during eval.
- Latency target: p95 < 300ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) and < 800ms for long sessions (>=750 tokens).
- Batch sizing: dynamic batching with 50ms scheduling window.

Modeling summary (quick):
- 8 GPUs: supports ~120 concurrent slots (p95 exceed target on long sessions), cost-efficient for a narrow eval only.
- 12 GPUs: ~190 concurrent slots, p95 close to target with optimistic cache behavior.
- 16 GPUs: ~280–320 concurrent slots, reliable to hit p95 targets across session length distribution with modest autoscale headroom.

Recommendation: proceed with a 16-GPU committed tranche for the initial reserved block if you expect the eval to stress both short and long sessions. That lets you run production-like load tests and keeps the procurement ask reasonable. If procurement prefers a phased approach, we can do 12 GPU + 4 GPU burst buffer (staged tranches) — procurement can sign the larger PO but invoice tranches on activation.

I'll bring the detailed latency curves to the infra sync.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Procurement Team <procurement@healthsync.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-08T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan kickoff — HealthSync evaluation

Thanks for the clarity and the attachments. Procurement reviewed the PO appendix and the acceptance checklist; a few commercial asks before we can circulate to finance:

- Can Redwood accept staged invoicing tied to tranche activation (we prefer that vs. single up-front invoice)?
- We need a 45-day remediation window in the acceptance appendix for critical defects discovered during onboarding testing.
- Please provide SOC2 auditor contact info and a redacted sample of your audit report delivery timeframe.

We are okay with an initial 12 GPU tranche with conditional burst to 16 for the eval if you can commit to the tranche activation windows you listed. We'll target internal approvals by 2026-10-15 and aim to sign the PO the week of 2026-10-18. Can you confirm whether a VPC deployment would reduce our lead time to the 6–8 week band?

Sienna will coordinate the infra sync; please send an invite for 2026-10-12 or 2026-10-13.

Procurement Team
